sources.locator: Institutional record abstract; publisher abstract search result; methods section 'Equilibration of Crackerbread to different aw levels' was visible only in indexed result excerpt. sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Crackerbread samples equilibrated across aw 0.113–0.98; 5 mm cylindrical probe with Instron; force and acoustic signals captured together. sources.authors: G. Hough, M. Del Pilar Buera, J. Chirife, O. Moro

sources.title: Effect of morphology on water sorption in cellular solid foods. Part II: Sorption in cereal crackers
sources.authors: D.C. Esveld, R.G.M. van der Sman, M.M. Witek, C.W. Windt, H. van As, J.P.M. van Duynhoven, M.B.J. Meinders
sources.locator: Publisher abstract and methods excerpt (cracker composition, proofing time); retrieved in search result 2026-10-10T06:29:50Z. Direct ScienceDirect page open returned HTTP 403 at 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.
sources.observed_operation: Retrieved publisher search result with primary article abstract and indexed method details; did not retrieve full text.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Primary study compared crackers with fine/coarse morphology and used SPI-NMR moisture profiles. The article reports morphology-dependent vapor conductivity and sorption kinetics, including about threefold faster local sorption in the fine-structure cracker at low aw. Its own authors caution against generalizing complex structure-dependent transport without product-specific characterization.
sources.applicability: Supports recording geometry and considering product-specific starting moisture gradients and kinetics. Specific morphology, recipe, and rates are not transferable.

sources.title: Selecting packaging material for dry food products by trade-off of sustainability and performance: a case study on cookies and milk powder
sources.version_or_release: Published article, Packaging Technology and Science 34(5), 303–318 (2021); DOI 10.1002/pts.2561
sources.locator: Ghent University Academic Bibliography abstract, lines 14–27 and citation/version record lines 54–57; opened 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z. Record lists full-text download, but downloaded/read version not used.
sources.observed_operation: Opened institutional bibliographic record and read abstract; direct download link was not followed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Caramelized cookies were flow-packed in PP (reported WVTR 5 g/m2/day), acryl-coated PVdC/PP (4.2), or metallized PP (0.4); stored 22 C/50% RH; the first two lost textural acceptability by six months while MPP extended it. Abstract does not report the WVTR test condition, full pouch dimensions, seal details, or exact acceptance method. A second powder comparison showed humidity-related barrier differences but is not a cookie result.
sources.applicability: Shows comparable constructions and real storage condition, and that barrier choice can alter performance in a specific cookie. Do not compare its WVTR numbers to a supplier datasheet without matched test conditions or transfer its six-month outcome.

sources.title: Chemical and physical changes during storage of differently packed biscuits formulated with sunflower oil
sources.authors: F. Balestra, V. Verardo, S. Tappi, M.F. Caboni, M. Dalla Rosa, S. Romani
sources.version_or_release: Version of record published 2019-07-05; Journal of Food Science and Technology 56, 4714–4721; DOI 10.1007/s13197-019-03918-z
sources.locator: PMC full-text indexed article result, Materials and methods (formulation, packaging materials, experimental conditions, analytical determinations) and abstract; retrieved 2026-10-10T06:30:46Z. Publisher version-of-record page opened 2026-10-10T06:28:34Z; direct PMC open returned recaptcha at 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.
sources.observed_operation: Retrieved full primary-article content in PMC indexed result and read publisher version-of-record abstract and metadata; the direct PMC page open was blocked by recaptcha.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Same production batch was randomly divided among three materials. Control was metalized OPP/paper; variants replaced the OPP layer with PLA or added EVA to OPP. Bags averaged 300 g filled product and 1,078 cm2 surface area. Accelerated storage was 35 C/50% RH for 105 days; samples were taken at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 85, 105 days. Abstract reports packaging material did not significantly change texture despite differences in moisture, aw, and oxidation indicators.
sources.applicability: Demonstrates controlled batch splitting, construction disclosure, and the need to measure texture separately from moisture. Formulation, accelerated conditions, materials, and duration differ from this case.

sources.title: Delayed Quality Deterioration of Low-Moisture Cereal-Based Snack by Storing in an Active Filler-Embedded LDPE Zipper Bag
sources.authors: Y. Jo, E. Kim, S. Kim, C. Ban, S. Lim
sources.version_or_release: Foods 11(12), 1704 (published 2022-06-10); DOI 10.3390/foods11121704; CC BY open article
sources.locator: Full-text PDF: citation/publication lines 0–10; bag materials/making lines 89–121; film vapor test/storage conditions lines 134–159; moisture/activity/texture methods lines 167–187; retrieved 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z.

sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Filler-embedded LDPE film was 40–45 micrometers; zipper bags were 25 x 30.5 cm and made with a continuous band heat sealer. Water-vapor flux was measured after 24 h at 25 C/50% RH using a 135 mL double-deionized-water cup. Snacks were stored at 25 C/50% RH for 1, 5, 10, 15, or 20 days; food type influenced outcomes. sources.title: BRICE project: Understanding checking and breakage of biscuits and dry cereal products
sources.authors: P. Le-Bail, M. Bedas, B. Jaillais, C. Jonchère, L. Ribourg, A.M. Le Bail
sources.version_or_release: Conference/proceedings paper in Cereal Foods World 64(6) (2019); no software-style commit applies

sources.observed_operation: Opened proceedings PDF and read project abstract; targeted publisher search result confirmed text.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Four-year project began in 2015. Study abstract compared round/thick biscuit with rectangular/thinner pierced biscuit; counted checking/breakage over 15 days; used Karl Fischer and automated NIR imaging for center/surface water; reports higher checking in the round/thick type and appearance within 1–2 days after baking. Detailed cooling line conditions are not disclosed in this short report.
sources.applicability: Supports the relevance of product geometry, moisture distribution, batch/shape tracking, and early observation points. It is an industry-collaborative comparator, not this snack or a film intervention.

sources.title: ASTM F88/F88M-23, Standard Test Method for Seal Strength of Flexible Barrier Materials
sources.version_or_release: F88/F88M-23, active version displayed by ASTM; DOI 10.1520/F0088_F0088M-23
sources.locator: ASTM catalog scope and significance/use sections; publisher page opened 2026-10-10T06:27:45Z. Summary lines in initial catalog result identify process validation/control/capability and force/failure mode.

sources.observed_operation: Opened official ASTM catalog summary; normative document not downloaded.

sources.title: Influence of Packaging Material/Sealing on the Quality of Biscuits
sources.authors: R.M. Vercelino Alves, E.E.C. Garcia, M.R. Bordin
sources.version_or_release: Research article, Journal of Plastic Film & Sheeting 15(1), 57–71; first published 1999-01; DOI 10.1177/875608799901500107
sources.locator: SAGE version-of-record page, abstract and publication metadata, lines 20–41 and 143–151; opened 2026-10-10T06:34:11Z.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official SAGE journal page and read abstract, film descriptions, observed package comparison, and publication metadata; full article is restricted.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Study assessed six biscuit wrapper structures: BOPP/pearlized BOPP, BOPP/BOPP, BOPP/LDPE/BOPP, BOPP/met-BOPP, BOPP/LDPE/met-BOPP, PET/met-BOPP. Compared measured whole-package water-vapor transmission with theoretical values for 9 retail biscuit types from 6 manufacturers made on 3 form-fill-seal machine types. Material WVTRs were reported at 38 C/90% RH. Rollpack and horizontal flowpack packages had impaired transverse-seal integrity and measured WVT 1.1–3.0 times theoretical; vertical-flowpack package seals were reported as good. Full methods not accessible in the page preview.
sources.applicability: A directly relevant failed package/seal comparator showing the finished package and seal can depart from a flat-film calculation. Machine outcomes are specific to the study and do not identify a fix or setting for the cooperative; no maintenance-cost evidence was reported.

sources.title: Interactions between water and EVOH food packaging films
sources.authors: S. Aucejo, R. Catalá, R. Gavara
sources.version_or_release: Research article, Food Science and Technology International 6(2), 159–164 (2000); DOI 10.1177/108201320000600211; first published 2000-04
sources.locator: SAGE version-of-record page, abstract lines 23–32 and publication metadata lines 197–209; opened 2026-10-10T06:35:18Z. Full article restricted.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official SAGE journal page and read the abstract and bibliographic metadata; full article not accessed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Four EVOH copolymers were tested by continuous-flow permeation and gravimetric experiments at different RH and 23 ± 2 C. Water permeability was approximately constant over aw 0.3–0.75, then increased by up to two orders of magnitude above aw 0.75; ethylene content changed uptake/permeability.
sources.applicability: A condition-specific material-layer caveat only if a proposed/current film actually contains EVOH; it demonstrates why a barrier value without RH/temperature and layer details can mislead. Does not establish the cooperative film structure or its water-vapor result.
